answer: Path-diversity weighting. Each agent's influence equals the number of disjoint routes its actions reach the wider graph through, counted over a rolling window. Every new identity must thread itself into existing traffic by relaying real transactions for honest clusters, and a cluster isolated on a single route (a canyon with no exits) gets its weight capped near zero. To fake breadth, an attacker must build and sustain separate live connections across many unrelated regions—each one a vine that costs bandwidth, uptime and genuine traffic—so weight grows only with real operational surface,
